$comment: HAND-MAINTAINED. The Atlas Cloud roster: which of Atlas's 473 models unmodel serves, and why.
WHY ATLAS AT ALL, recorded honestly. This provider was requested as a second transport for the
Seedance family — models unmodel already reaches at `bytedance.video` (ByteDance's own ModelArk)
and at `fal.video` (fal.ai's queue). The stated reason was moderation, and that reason is WRONG on
the public record: Atlas's own Seedance 2.5 page says "All uploaded portraits go through automatic
moderation. Non-compliant content will be blocked — not every image can be uploaded", and its
schema descriptions add "Images containing real human faces cannot be uploaded directly; use
model-generated assets, preset digital characters, or authorized real-person assets." fal's
`image_urls` carries no equivalent restriction. So Atlas moderates the reference-image path MORE
than fal does, not less. The durable reason is a PARTNER-TRANSPORT one — a contract designating
Atlas as the permitted vendor for these models — and it is recorded that way here so the next
reader who checks the moderation claim does not find this file wrong on its face.
THE LIBRARY REASON is independent of the contract and would justify the provider on its own: three
transports for one set of weights compile to three visibly different bodies, and feeding one to
another's validator fails. That is docs/decisions.md §1 working rather than redundancy — see the
diff table at the top of src/providers/atlascloud/video.ts.
SCOPE: VIDEO ONLY, hand-written, no generator. Atlas serves all media from three POST routes
(`/model/generateVideo`, `/generateImage`, `/generateAudio`) covering nine unmodel verbs, and its
`type`/`categories` taxonomy is too lossy to be the source of a verb map: seven `suno/chirp-*`
MUSIC models are filed under TEXT-TO-SPEECH, `tripo-h3.1/image-to-3d` is `type: "Image"`, and
`bytedance/seed-asr-2.0` (speech-to-text) is `type: "Audio"`. Hand curation is mandatory, exactly
as at fal.
`endpoints` — one entry per curated model id. The id is a real, REQUIRED BODY field rather than a
URL path: Atlas routes every video model through one url and `model` selects both the model and
the task, which is why there is no `endpoint` pseudo-param anywhere in this provider.
verb    REQUIRED. `video` on every row today — this provider serves one category.
route   text | image | reference. The id names it, and each route is its OWN OpenAPI document.
family  Atlas's own `familyName` from the catalog, verbatim.
note    what is unusual about this row.
Every id here resolves against the keyless catalog (GET https://api.atlascloud.ai/api/v1/models)
and against its own keyless schema (https://static.atlascloud.ai/model/schema/<id-with-dashes>.json),
and every schema is committed under data/atlascloud/openapi/. Verified live 2026-08-26: 473 rows
(Video 196 / Image 121 / Text 136 / Audio 20), 473/473 carrying a schema URL, robots.txt on the
schema host is `Allow: /`.
ROSTER SHAPE. 23 ids: the five Seedance families the adopter named (2.5 x3, 2.0 x3, 2.0-mini x3,
2.0-fast x3, v1.5-pro x4 = 16), plus the earners at the top of Atlas's own TEXT-TO-VIDEO /
IMAGE-TO-VIDEO listing — Wan 3.0 and Wan 3.0-prime (Atlas's highest-priority video rows, tagged
HOT + NEW; 4 ids) and Veo 3.1 (3 ids: a third transport for weights already at `google.video` and
`fal.video`, which is the sharpest same-weights-different-bodies comparison in the tree).
Atlas's genuine additions over fal's Seedance roster are the `-mini` tier and the SR/ESR
resolution ladder (11 resolutions on 2.5 against fal's 3).
NO GENERATOR IN THIS WAVE, and the promotion bar is recorded: `scripts/codegen-atlascloud.ts`
becomes worth ~1,500 LoC only past roughly 40 curated ids. It would also need two lowering rules
fal's codegen does not have — `allOf` + `if/then` conditionals become IR constraints instead of a
hard error (`google/veo3.1/*` has one: "When resolution is 1080p or 4k, duration must be 8") — and
the three-routes-to-nine-verbs mapping would have to come from THIS file, never from
`type`/`categories`.
DRIFT. `bun run audit:atlascloud` diffs the live catalog against this file and reports gone / new /
changed, and re-hashes every committed schema snapshot. It never writes. Atlas's doc rot is already
visible — the official video API reference sends `"model": "kling-v2.0"`, an id that is not in the
live catalog — so the gate is as mandatory here as at fal.

alibaba/wan-3.0-prime/image-to-video.note: No `ratio` field at all: the first frame decides the shape. `prompt` is REQUIRED here, unlike on the Seedance image routes where it is "Optional but recommended".

alibaba/wan-3.0-prime/text-to-video.note: Atlas's highest-priority video row (HOT + NEW). The ONE upper-case resolution enum on the provider: 1080P / 720P / 480P. Its audio toggle is `audio`, not `generate_audio`.

alibaba/wan-3.0/text-to-video.note: Same family, LOWER-case resolutions plus an `-esr` enhancement ladder the prime tier lacks — two spellings of one idea inside one family, which is why every table in this provider is per model.

bytedance/seedance-2.0-fast/text-to-vide.note: Byte-identical schema to the mini tier's, different weights and a different price — which is why the roster names both rather than one.

bytedance/seedance-2.0-mini/reference-to.note: As above, with the 9/3/3 reference caps.

bytedance/seedance-2.0-mini/text-to-vide.note: The `-mini` tier is one of Atlas's two genuine additions over fal's Seedance roster. No native 1080p: `1080p-SR` upscales a 720p render.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/image-to-video.note: First + last frame. `bitrate_mode` and `seed` are the 2.0 series' own fields; Seedance 2.5 has neither.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/reference-to-vide.note: Reference caps are a third of 2.5's (9/3/3), and `minItems` is 1 rather than 0 — an empty array is a schema violation here and legal on 2.5.

bytedance/seedance-2.0/text-to-video.note: The only Seedance on Atlas with NATIVE 4k: "'4k' is native UHD (3840x2160, 16:9) available on the full Seedance 2.0 models only (not Fast/Mini)".

bytedance/seedance-2.5/image-to-video.note: The one row in the roster whose `ratio` enum has a single member: "Seedance 2.5 image-to-video (first-frame and first+last-frame) accepts only 'adaptive': the output preserves the source image's aspect ratio."

bytedance/seedance-2.5/reference-to-vide.note: The richest row: reference_images (<=30), reference_videos (<=10), reference_audios (<=10), audio-only referencing (unique to 2.5), `omni_reference_task_type`, and the 11-value SR/ESR resolution ladder. This is the id the adopter asked for by name.

bytedance/seedance-2.5/text-to-video.note: Seedance 2.5 text-to-video. `duration` is an INTEGER enum [-1, 4..30] whose -1 means "the model picks the length" — the same sentinel ModelArk documents, and the one fal's string enum spells "auto".

bytedance/seedance-v1.5-pro/image-to-vid.note: Doc rot recorded: its schema describes `image` and `last_image` as "The positive prompt for the generation" — a copy-paste from `prompt`.

bytedance/seedance-v1.5-pro/text-to-vide.note: The family that breaks the house dialect: `aspect_ratio` rather than `ratio`, `camera_fixed`, a [4,12] RANGE rather than an enum, and NO -1 sentinel.
720p only, where the non-fast pair also renders 480p.

google/veo3.1/image-to-video.note: As above. `generate_audio` defaults to FALSE here and to true on every Seedance row — same field name, opposite default.

google/veo3.1/reference-to-video.note: Its reference array is `images` (1-3), not `reference_images`. Two Atlas schema bugs recorded: `x-order-properties` lists an `aspect_ratio` that `properties` does not declare, and a stray top-level `seed` object sits beside `properties`.

google/veo3.1/text-to-video.note: The third transport for Veo 3.1 (also `google.video` natively and `fal.video` on the queue). Carries the roster's only `allOf` + `if/then` conditional: "When resolution is 1080p or 4k, duration must be 8 (seconds)."

$comment: Deliberate exclusions carry recorded reasons (docs/decisions.md §6).
`categories` is a map of ATLAS TAXONOMY KEYS to the reason that whole slice is out, and it is
DOCUMENTATION — nothing reads it at run time. That is deliberate rather than an oversight: Atlas's
own categories are not trustworthy enough to gate on (suno music under TEXT-TO-SPEECH, Tripo 3D
under `type: "Image"`, seed-asr speech-to-text under `type: "Audio"`), so enforcement is by ID in
`endpoints` below and in `src/providers/atlascloud/models.ts`, which is the only list a request can
actually be checked against.

categories.AUDIO-TO-VIDEO: 4 rows. Audio-driven video is `unmodel/lipsync` and `unmodel/avatar` territory, and neither vocabulary has been checked against Atlas's schemas.
categories.IMAGE-TO-IMAGE: Same route, same reason; also where Atlas files its upscalers.
categories.SPEECH-TO-TEXT: `/model/generateAudio`, and mis-typed: `bytedance/seed-asr-2.0` is `type: "Audio"` on a route that also serves TTS and music.
categories.TEXT-TO-3D: 3D is a later wave library-wide (`unmodel/3d` has two providers today). Atlas files `tripo-h3.1/text-to-3d` under `type: "Image"`, which is the taxonomy problem in one row.
categories.TEXT-TO-IMAGE: `/model/generateImage` is a second route with its own per-model schemas. Real work, not blocked — deliberately out of a video-only wave.
categories.TEXT-TO-SPEECH: Blocked on curation, not on effort: `elevenlabs/v3/text-to-speech` exposes `voice` as an enum of 21 raw opaque ids (`hpp4J3VqNfWAUOO0d1Us`, ...) with no names, and shipping that enum verbatim violates "autocomplete is the product". The slice also mis-files seven `suno/chirp-*` MUSIC models under this key, so it cannot even be read as a TTS list. Hand-curated voice rows first, then a wave.
categories.VIDEO-TO-VIDEO: 17 rows Atlas files here (restyle, upscale, extend). unmodel reaches the Seedance video-editing path through the `/reference-to-video` ids and their `omni_reference_task_type`, which is where Atlas actually implements it; the rest are upscale/restyle verbs that would need their own curation.

endpoints.atlascloud/chat (the 136 rows at api.atl: NOT a media route at all: Atlas serves chat from `https://api.atlascloud.ai/v1` in the OpenAI dialect, with an OpenRouter-shaped keyless catalog (`context_length`, `max_output_length`, `input_modalities`, `supported_features`, per-token `pricing`). That is an `openai-compatible` overlay plus a generated catalog — a cheaper and completely separate effort. `data/models-dev.json` has no Atlas entry (184 providers, zero matches), so `/v1/models` would have to be the catalog source. Recorded as the obvious next Atlas wave, not as a gap in this one.
endpoints.elevenlabs/v3/text-to-speech: The autocomplete hazard, by name: `voice` is 21 opaque ElevenLabs ids with no display names. unmodel serves ElevenLabs natively with hand-curated voice rows; an Atlas resale carrying raw ids would be strictly worse than what already ships.
endpoints.kwaivgi/kling-v3.0-*, kwaivgi/kling-v2.6: Kling on Atlas is 12+ video routes (pro / std / turbo / 4k, motion-control, avatar) and unmodel already serves Kling natively (`kling.video` and four siblings) and at fal. A Kling-on-Atlas sweep is a roster decision of its own rather than a backfill; recorded so the next widening starts from a decision rather than from whichever id someone asks for first.
endpoints.minimax/h3/{text,image,reference}-to-vid: An earner, and still excluded. Its `refers` field is an ARRAY OF TYPED OBJECTS (`{ url, type?: image|video|audio }`) rather than the three flat string arrays that are this provider's whole shape story, and it requires `duration` and `resolution` on every call. That is a fifth reference vocabulary in a provider curated for having one, and unmodel already reaches MiniMax-H3 twice — natively at `minimax.videoV2` and on fal's queue at `minimax/h3/*` — so a third transport buys the least of any row considered. Reconsider if the `refers` shape spreads to other Atlas models.
endpoints.suno/chirp-*: Seven MUSIC models Atlas files under TEXT-TO-SPEECH. Excluded twice over: wrong category in the source data, and music is not this wave.
endpoints.xai/grok-imagine-video*, alibaba/happyho: Uncurated video rows in categories this provider already serves. Left out on the CHEAPNESS bar the fal roster uses — a row joins when it resolves live, its price is transcribable, and it lowers into an existing shape class with no new generator work. These fail the middle clause: Atlas publishes no usable price UNIT for any of them (see data/atlascloud/pricing.json), so all 23 curated ids already ship unpriced, and widening the roster widens that hole faster than it widens the surface. `bun run audit:atlascloud` lists them every week.
